_metadata.description: Verified diversion program eligibility by state. Claude references this instead of generating program names/eligibility from memory.
_metadata.anti_hallucination: If a program or jurisdiction is not in this file, the report MUST say: 'Diversion program eligibility varies by county and State Attorney's office — ask your attorney about available alternatives.'

pretrial_intervention_felony.name: Pretrial Intervention Program (PTI) — Felony
pretrial_intervention_felony.description: Diversion program allowing eligible defendants to avoid prosecution by completing supervision and conditions
pretrial_intervention_felony.eligible_charges: Generally non-violent felonies where defendant has no prior felony convictions
general_eligibility: Victim and State Attorney must consent
disqualifiers: Trafficking charges (generally ineligible without special State Attorney approval)
pretrial_intervention_felony.completion_result: Charges dismissed (nolle prosequi) upon successful completion
pretrial_intervention_felony.typical_duration: 6-12 months (can be up to 1 year for felonies)
pretrial_intervention_felony.county_variation: Eligibility criteria and available programs vary significantly by judicial circuit and State Attorney's office

pretrial_intervention_misdemeanor.name: Misdemeanor Pretrial Intervention
pretrial_intervention_misdemeanor.description: Similar to felony PTI but for misdemeanor charges
pretrial_intervention_misdemeanor.eligible_charges: Misdemeanors where defendant has no prior convictions

drug_court.name: Drug Court / Treatment-Based Drug Court Program
drug_court.description: Intensive treatment program as alternative to incarceration for substance abuse-related offenses
eligible_charges: Some property crimes driven by substance abuse
disqualifiers: Drug trafficking (generally NOT eligible — trafficking penalties are statutory mandatory minimums)
Prior drug court failure (varies by circuit)
drug_court.completion_result: Varies by circuit — may result in charges dismissed, reduced charges, or reduced sentence
drug_court.note: Drug court availability and eligibility vary dramatically by county. Some circuits have very active programs; others are limited.

veterans_treatment_court.name: Veterans Treatment Court
veterans_treatment_court.statute: F.S. § 394.47891 (Veterans Treatment Court) and F.S. § 948.08(7) (veteran PTI)
veterans_treatment_court.description: Specialized court for veterans with service-connected mental health or substance abuse issues
veterans_treatment_court.eligible_charges: Varies by circuit — generally non-violent offenses with demonstrated connection to military service-related conditions
general_eligibility: Veteran or active duty service member
Condition connected to military service (PTSD, TBI, substance abuse, mental health)
veterans_treatment_court.completion_result: Varies — may include charge dismissal, reduced charges, or alternative sentencing
veterans_treatment_court.county_variation: Not available in all circuits. Check local availability.

mental_health_court.name: Mental Health Court
mental_health_court.description: Specialized court for defendants with diagnosed mental health conditions
mental_health_court.eligible_charges: Varies by circuit — generally non-violent offenses where mental health condition is a contributing factor

dui_diversion.name: DUI Diversion / First-Time DUI Program
dui_diversion.description: Alternative to standard DUI prosecution for first-time offenders
dui_diversion.eligible_charges: First DUI offense with no aggravating factors
general_eligibility: BAC below certain threshold (varies by program)
disqualifiers: Refusal to submit to testing (in some circuits)
dui_diversion.completion_result: Charges reduced or dismissed (varies by circuit)
dui_diversion.county_variation: NOT available in all Florida counties. Many circuits do NOT offer DUI diversion. Check local availability.

youthful_offender.name: Youthful Offender Sentencing
youthful_offender.description: Alternative sentencing for defendants under age 21 at time of offense
general_eligibility: Under 21 years old at time of offense
Not charged with capital or life felony
Not previously classified as youthful offender
Judge or State Attorney must designate
youthful_offender.max_sentence: 6 years (regardless of statutory maximum for the offense)
youthful_offender.note: Youthful offender designation is discretionary — not automatic even if criteria are met

substantial_assistance.name: Substantial Assistance (Cooperation)
substantial_assistance.statute: F.S. § 893.135(4) (trafficking); general authority under sentencing statutes
substantial_assistance.description: The ONLY mechanism to go below mandatory minimum sentences in Florida trafficking cases
substantial_assistance.how_it_works: The STATE must file the motion — the judge cannot depart from the mandatory minimum without the State's motion. Defendant provides cooperation (testimony, information, undercover work) in exchange for the State's recommendation for reduced sentence.
substantial_assistance.note: This is not a 'program' — it is a prosecutorial tool. The defendant has no right to substantial assistance; it is entirely at the State Attorney's discretion.
risks: Safety risk to defendant and family
Cooperation may be insufficient (State determines adequacy)
Cooperation may not result in the reduction defendant expects
Information provided can be used against defendant if cooperation fails
